Passengers settled into worn velvet seats while the conductor collected tickets with practiced ease. Beyond the window, fishing boats drifted toward the open water as gulls circled above the lighthouse. A retired cartographer sat across the aisle, unfolding a creased map of the northern provinces. She traced the river valleys with her finger and described the ruined abbeys hidden among the hills. The train climbed slowly past orchards heavy with autumn apples and meadows where horses grazed beside stone walls. At the border town, a museum curator boarded carrying a leather satchel full of ancient coins. He explained how each coin revealed the trade routes of a forgotten empire. Children pressed their faces to the glass as the viaduct carried them above a deep green gorge. A waterfall tumbled down the far cliff while mist rose through the pine forest below. The dining car served strong coffee and warm bread as the afternoon light turned golden. An astronomer traveling to the mountain observatory spoke about the coming meteor shower. She predicted clear skies and described the constellations visible from the summit. Outside, villages with red tiled roofs gave way to dense oak woodland. Sheep dotted the higher pastures where shepherds watched from stone huts. The engine slowed near a lakeside halt where swans gathered among the reeds. Vendors sold roasted chestnuts and woven scarves on the platform. A historian opposite opened a journal filled with sketches of medieval bridges. He compared the arches of distant cities and noted the masons who carved them. Rain began to patter against the windows as the valley narrowed into a rocky defile. Thunder echoed faintly while the lights flickered on inside the carriage. The cartographer pointed out the fortress crowning the next ridge, its towers dark against the clouds. She recalled the siege that ended there three centuries ago. The train emerged onto a wide plain where windmills turned above fields of barley. Distant mountains showed their first snow along the highest ridges. Evening approached as the city finally appeared on the horizon. Street lamps glowed along the boulevards and the cathedral bells rang out. The travelers gathered their luggage and exchanged addresses with promises to write. The station clock showed half past seven as the brakes sighed to a stop.
